content: An audio clip of the word “Laurel" gained widespread attention in 2018, with coverage by notable news outlets such as The New York Times and Time. Roughly half of listeners perceive “Laurel” and the other half perceive “Yanny” or similar-sounding words, with high confidence on both sides BIBREF1 . One of the reasons the public was intrigued is because examples of such phenomena are viewed as rare, isolated instances. In a preliminary attempt to investigate the density of such phenomena, we identified five additional distinct examples (Table 7 ). The supplementary files include 10 versions of one of these examples, where listeners tend to perceive either “worlds” or “yikes.” Across the different audio clips, one should be able to hear both interpretations. The threshold for switching from one interpretation to another differs from person to person.
